newsitem.title: UK: Lubricants lift profits at Britain's Burmah.
newsitem.headline: Lubricants lift profits at Britain's Burmah.

text.p: The British lubricants and chemicals firm Burmah Castrol reported a 13 percent profit rise Monday as its Asian lubricants operations continued to power ahead.
Net attributable income climbed to 67.7 million pounds ($105.4 million) from 59.9 million ($93 million) as Castrol lubricant volumes climbed 10 percent in Asia -- double the rate of market growth.
The profit figure excludes a 23.2 million pound ($36 million) gain stemming from the sale of fuels operations in Sweden, Turkey and Chile earlier this year.
Chief Executive Jonathan Fry told Reuters that Asia would remain the main drive behind Burmah's results, thanks to the popularity of the Castrol brand name and the firm's experience in the region.

"It is a considerably successful story. We've got a lot of momentum there," Fry said. "It's really our understanding of the markets. We were in a number of them very early and our brand is very popular," he added.
Burmah expanded its Asian operations in June, when it set up a joint venture to target the fast growing Chinese lubricants market.

With the Brazilian lubricants operations led by a new management team and on track to become profitable again next year, Burmah only needs a pick-up in the German economy to power full steam ahead, Fry said.
Chemicals and lubricants are Burmah's core businesses. For some time Burmah has been negotiating to divest its Pakistani gas investments.
